premise: defect: process is documented as an instance of EventEmitter; node:events semantics (duplicate listeners, listenerCount(ev, fn), errorMonitor, emit('error') with no listener throws, borrowed EventEmitter.prototype methods operate on the same registry) are the contract. Bun's process used a separate native emitter (WebCore::JSEventEmitter) that reimplements these and diverges.
pick_reason: process becomes a real node:events EventEmitter: its prototype inherits from EventEmitter.prototype and its listeners live in its own _events. One implementation of the emitter contract is left, so every divergence of the native copy (dedupe, listenerCount(ev, fn), errorMonitor, no-listener error, throwing listeners, removeListener meta event, borrowed methods, process.on !== EventEmitter.prototype.on) ends at once, and about 1,600 lines of native emitter are deleted. Runtime-started emits (signals, IPC, exit, warnings) call the same emit.
why_not_minimal: The minimal patch (oven-sh/bun#41830) repairs three symptoms inside the native emitter and leaves a second implementation of the EventEmitter contract that still differs (borrowed methods use another registry, emit does not propagate a throw, no 'removeListener' event, no rawListeners wrappers). Each new difference needs another native patch. It also keeps the cost of the native emitter: binary bytes and a separate listener map.
plan: One PR. The methods of EventEmitter.prototype live in the internal module internal/events/prototype (not builtins): --compile --bytecode embeds bytecode for internal modules only (#40794).
EventEmitter.prototype is a native object with a lazy static property table: a method is read from the module at its first read, so the first access of process evaluates nothing.

Process inherits from it, listeners live in process._events, signal/IPC/memoryPressure hooks are 'newListener'/'removeListener' listeners as in node, the native emitter is deleted. Carries the tests of #41830.

Runtime emits call process.emit (own or inherited) when it is not the emit of node:events: fixes #12918 (#29194, #32227). With the default emit and no listener nothing is called and no module is evaluated.
A worker's 'exit' listeners run before the VM is marked shutting down (web_worker.rs), so what one throws is reported like on the main thread.
bun test exits 1 when an 'exit' listener throws (the 5 lines of #41588).

build_findings: An eager prototype (19 builtin functions, 18 property transitions) made the first access of process cost 146k instructions (base 50.5k). The lazy table makes it 37.8k.
A static-table entry with a getter or setter would flag the structure (or, with Bun's stale lut generator, fail on assignment): all entries are PropertyCallback.

Bun's lut generator never sets HashTable::seenPropertyAttributes: process.exitCode = x only worked because the old native prototype had a custom accessor. Process::createStructure now sets the flag. Handed off the generator fix.
emit without a rest parameter (arguments object) is 3x to 15x slower in FTL for more than three arguments and for 'error': kept the closure that a builtin returns.
Cost that stays: the first process.on() of a program that used no EventEmitter before compiles addListener and emit: 634k instructions (base 10.5k).

Self-review of the builtins design (verdict rework): builtin functions get no embedded bytecode under --compile --bytecode (first on/emit/off 233,812 -> 1,009,256 instructions, 6 -> 20 source parses), and it added a cross-cutting builtins mechanism plus ZigGlobalObject fields. The module design removes all of that.

Worker: web_worker.rs set is_shutting_down before on_exit(), so VirtualMachine::uncaught_exception dropped what an 'exit' listener throws. Removed the early set: the main thread sets it after the listeners too.
